theory.title: Talking about your life and experiences
theory.explanation: Usamos el present perfect para hablar de experiencias y situaciones conectadas con el presente cuando no decimos cuándo ocurrieron: I've visited Scotland. Si indicamos un momento pasado terminado, usamos past simple: I visited Scotland in 2023. En preguntas de experiencia usamos ever; para decir que nunca hemos hecho algo, usamos never. Already y just suelen aparecer antes del participio; yet suele ir al final de preguntas y negativas. For introduce una duración y since un punto de inicio. Para contar una historia, combinamos past simple y past continuous y ordenamos los hechos con first, then, after that, while y finally. Used to describe hábitos o estados del pasado que ya no son habituales.
theory.tip: No combines present perfect con un momento pasado terminado como yesterday, last year o in 2022. Di I've travelled abroad (experiencia) o I travelled abroad last year (momento terminado).

patterns.label: Present perfect: experience
patterns.pattern: Have/has + past participle; no se indica cuándo ocurrió.
examples: I've visited Ireland twice.
Have/has + past participle; no se indica cuándo ocurrió.

patterns.label: Past simple: finished time
patterns.pattern: Usa el pasado simple con un momento terminado.
examples: I visited Ireland in 2022.
Usa el pasado simple con un momento terminado.

patterns.label: Contrast: life experience vs finished event
patterns.pattern: Present perfect para experiencia; past simple para el detalle fechado.
examples: I've been to Rome. I went there last May.
Present perfect para experiencia; past simple para el detalle fechado.

patterns.label: Ever and never
patterns.pattern: Ever aparece en preguntas de experiencia; never expresa «nunca».
examples: Have you ever flown? I've never flown.
Ever aparece en preguntas de experiencia; never expresa «nunca».

patterns.label: Already, just and yet
patterns.pattern: Already/just suelen ir entre have y el participio; yet suele ir al final.
examples: I've already eaten. She's just arrived. We haven't left yet.
Already/just suelen ir entre have y el participio; yet suele ir al final.

patterns.label: For and since
patterns.pattern: For + duración; since + punto de inicio.
examples: I've studied English for six years. I've studied it since 2020.
For + duración; since + punto de inicio.

patterns.label: Past continuous with past simple
patterns.pattern: Past continuous describe el fondo; past simple, el evento que interrumpe.
examples: I was walking home when it started to rain.
Past continuous describe el fondo; past simple, el evento que interrumpe.

patterns.label: Used to for past habits
patterns.pattern: Used to + infinitivo describe hábitos o estados pasados que cambiaron.
examples: I used to live in a small town.
Used to + infinitivo describe hábitos o estados pasados que cambiaron.

patterns.label: Narrative sequence
patterns.pattern: Ordena acontecimientos con first, then, after that, while y finally.
examples: First, we arrived; then, we checked in.
Ordena acontecimientos con first, then, after that, while y finally.

patterns.label: Present perfect negative and questions
patterns.pattern: Have/has + not + participio; invierte have/has en preguntas.
examples: I haven't finished. Have you finished yet?
Have/has + not + participio; invierte have/has en preguntas.

content.passage: When Sofia finished university, she wanted to do something different. She had always been interested in other cultures, so she decided to travel abroad for a few months. At first, she felt nervous because she had never travelled alone. However, she soon made friends at a language course in Edinburgh. She has kept in touch with some of them ever since. Last summer, Sofia returned to Scotland to visit her friends. They spent a week exploring the city and talking about their experiences. Sofia has learned that travelling can make people more independent. She has also improved her English and become more confident. She hasn't decided where to go next yet, but she is already looking for another opportunity. Looking back, she feels proud of the choices she has made.

items.prompt: Describe an important experience in your life. Include when it happened and why it mattered.
items.modelAnswer: One important experience in my life was travelling to Ireland two years ago. I went there with a friend and stayed for a week. I've never forgotten the people we met.

items.prompt: Talk about something you have achieved recently.
items.modelAnswer: Recently, I've completed an online course. It was a challenge because I had to study after work, but I'm proud of the progress I've made.

items.prompt: Describe a place you visited in the past and what you did there.
items.modelAnswer: I visited Edinburgh last summer. I explored the old town, visited museums and tried local food. I enjoyed the trip because I learned a lot about Scottish culture.

items.prompt: Talk about a skill you have improved over time.
items.modelAnswer: I've improved my English over the last two years. I practise a little every day and I take part in a conversation group once a week.

items.prompt: Describe a person who has influenced you.
items.modelAnswer: My older sister has influenced me a lot. When I was younger, she encouraged me to try new things. I've learned to be more confident from her.

items.prompt: Compare your life now with your life when you were younger.
items.modelAnswer: When I was younger, I used to spend more time outdoors. Now I work and study, so my routine is busier. However, I still make time for friends.

items.prompt: Tell a short story about a problem you had during a journey.
items.modelAnswer: Last year, I was travelling by train when the service stopped. At first, I felt worried, but a member of staff helped us find another route.

items.prompt: Explain why you would like to travel abroad.
items.modelAnswer: I'd like to travel abroad because I'm interested in other cultures. I haven't visited Japan yet, and I'd like to learn more about its history.

items.prompt: Talk about something you have never done but would like to try.
items.modelAnswer: I've never tried scuba diving, but I'd like to do it one day. It looks challenging and I think it would be an unforgettable experience.

items.prompt: Give a two-minute summary of your life so far, using past events and present experiences.
items.modelAnswer: So far, I've had many interesting experiences. I grew up in a small town, studied at university and started working a few years ago. I've met people who have helped me become more independent. One important moment was moving to a new city. At first it was difficult, but eventually I felt at home.

content.audioTranscript: Daniel: Have you ever travelled abroad? Laura: Yes, I have. I visited Portugal last year. Daniel: Where did you stay? Laura: I stayed in Lisbon for five days. Daniel: What did you enjoy most? Laura: I tried local food and met friendly people. Daniel: Have you travelled anywhere else? Laura: I haven't travelled to Italy yet, but I've been to France twice. Daniel: How long have you been interested in travel? Laura: I've been interested in other cultures since I was a child. Daniel: What have you learned from your trips? Laura: I've learned to be more independent.
